title: Human CSF Processing for 10x scRNA-seq
author: Le Zhang
materials: 10x Genomics Chromium Single Cell 5' Reagent Kit v2

steps.title: Collect CSF and handle waste
steps.instruction: Perform lumbar puncture using a Sprotte atraumatic needle with cannula; if bleeding occurs, collect the first 1–2 mL of CSF into a CSF WASTE tube. Continue drawing CSF until it is visibly free of red blood cells, then collect up to 30 mL into pre‑labeled tubes (proceed even if less is obtained). Replace caps and gently invert each tube 3–4 times. Keep all samples on ice or at 4 °C after collection. Collect the CSF at room temperature (64–77 °F / 18–25 °C) and note that no fasting is required.

substeps.instruction: Perform lumbar puncture with Sprotte atraumatic needle.
If bleeding, collect first 1–2 mL in CSF WASTE tube.
Continue collection until CSF is clear of RBCs.
Collect up to 30 mL into pre‑labeled tubes; proceed if less.
Keep samples on ice or at 4 °C.

steps.title: Record sample metadata
steps.instruction: Record the total CSF volume, note any visible RBC contamination or pink/red hue, and document the date and time of collection.

steps.title: Transport CSF to laboratory
steps.instruction: Transfer the CSF sample to the laboratory as quickly as possible for processing.

steps.title: First centrifugation of CSF cells
steps.instruction: Spin the CSF at 300 × g, 4 °C for 10 minutes using a swing‑bucket centrifuge.

steps.title: Aspirate supernatant and preserve
steps.instruction: Using a pipette, aspirate the supernatant leaving approximately 500 µL without disturbing the cell pellet; keep the removed supernatant on ice for later aliquots.

steps.title: Count total CSF cells
steps.instruction: Mix the cell suspension gently, take 5 µL, dilute 1:1 with trypan blue, and count cells using a C‑Chip disposable hemacytometer (catalog DHCN015); record the total cell number.

steps.title: Second spin of cell suspension
steps.instruction: Transfer the cell suspension to a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube and spin at 300 × g, 4 °C for 10 minutes using a swing‑bucket centrifuge.

steps.title: Remove excess supernatant
steps.instruction: Carefully aspirate the supernatant, leaving approximately 50 µL with the cell pellet.

steps.title: Resuspend and adjust cell concentration
steps.instruction: Resuspend the cells in the remaining volume and recount; if a lower concentration is required, add CSF supernatant to dilute.

steps.title: Load cells onto 10x Chromium
steps.instruction: Aim for a concentration of 700–1200 cells/µL; if cell numbers are low, load the entire 50 µL. Use the 10x Genomics Chromium Single Cell 5' Reagent Kit v2 chemistry for single‑cell gene expression and TCR/BCR sequencing.

steps.title: Freeze leftover cells
steps.instruction: If cells remain after loading, spin at 400 × g, 4 °C for 5 minutes using a swing‑bucket centrifuge, resuspend the pellet in 0.1 mL Bambanker cell freezing medium, place the tube in a Mr. Frosty container at –80 °C, and after 24–72 hours transfer to a liquid N₂ tank.
